plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and large, rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is a classic winter bloomer in gardens, valued for brightening the cold season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak in winter)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant from which all true tea is made.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing perennial with nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that have golden stamens. It blooms in the cold of winter, often pushing up through frost and snow in woodland gardens.
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; grown in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with huge, artichoke-like flower heads surrounded by showy bracts. In the Southern Hemisphere it flowers during the summer months and is the largest of all proteas.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowers also appearing around the new year
plants.location: Fynbos region of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of South Africa, and its flower heads can reach 30 cm in diameter.

plants.name: Jasminum nudiflorum
plants.description: A deciduous, arching shrub that produces bright yellow flowers on bare green stems in winter. It is exceptionally hardy and is commonly trained along walls and fences.
plants.location: Native to northern China; naturalized and cultivated across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Unlike many jasmines, its flowers have little or no fragrance, but they can bloom in snow.
